objective.name: Change the training objective
objective.summary: Pointwise BCE optimises a different thing from a within-user ranking metric. Pairwise (BPR) or listwise (softmax over the user's list) targets the metric directly.
notes: SPLIT into concrete children: objective_listwise, objective_bpr, objective_hybrid_listwise. Consult those before proposing anything here.
The organizers rank this their most likely direction, and it is the only one that has produced a verified shippable gain -- but only in one of nine implementations.

sequence.name: User behaviour sequences / target attention
sequence.summary: No behaviour sequence is used at all. DIN/SIM-style interest modelling over the user history is unexplored.
notes: Check history_coverage first: attention needs the candidate or its author to actually appear in the user history.

multitask.name: Multi-task auxiliary heads
multitask.summary: is_click, is_like, play_time_ms and others are available as auxiliary targets while long_view stays the scored task.
notes: Reach them with harness.adapter.auxiliary_targets(). Never same-row inputs.

watchtime.name: Censored watch-time regression
watchtime.summary: A completed play truncates true watch time, so a one-sided loss rather than squared error.
notes: Needs play_time_ms and duration_ms via the adapter.

model_family.name: Different model family
model_family.summary: DeepFM / DCN / xDeepFM / GBDT over engineered features.
notes: The organizers deprioritise this because capacity measurably is not the bottleneck — see the capacity dead end.

temporal.name: Time features and drift
temporal.summary: hourmin, date, and the train-to-validation regime change.
notes: Daily volume collapses 13.6x INSIDE the training window (4/11 peak, 4/19 trough), not at the train/validation boundary.

debias.name: Exposure debiasing / unbiased validation
debias.summary: The random-exposure log as an unbiased check on a model fitted to biased traffic.
notes: is_rand is 0 on every standard-log row, so it carries no propensity signal there. The random log has no rows before 20220422.

ensembling.name: Variance reduction / ensembling
ensembling.summary: Combine several independently-seeded models' within-user ranks to cancel the per-seed embedding-noise term.
notes: Kept, but the gain is BELOW the 0.002 practical epsilon: +0.00112 mean over 3 matched seeds, worst +0.00090, all positive. Treat as a reliable small top-up, not as a direction that can carry a run on its own. See constraints.md C30.

Clears the UNANIMOUS_ACCEPT bar (0.0008), not the single-measurement ACCEPT bar (0.0014): mean +0.00112 with all three matched seeds positive. Under the old bar this node was reverted out of the lineage despite being the highest-scoring node of the project -- see BUGS.md F19.
Five identity seeds give a validation population std of 0.00032.
The harness also runs a zero-token rank-average ensembler on a fixed cadence, so proposing a plain seed-average duplicates something already free.

measured.note: 5-model average over the kept feature set; per-seed 0.60699/0.60723/0.60741

static_features.name: Add more static categorical fields
static_features.summary: Extending the FM from 5 fields to the 13 CWM fields.
notes: Organizer-published. Within noise and slightly worse. Reproducible via ablation_features.py — do not run it, it scores test.

capacity.name: Increase embedding dimension
capacity.summary: Larger k for the factorization machine.
notes: Organizer-published. Capacity is not the bottleneck; 1.14M rows do not support more of it.

user_side_first_order.name: Pure user-side first-order features
user_side_first_order.summary: A user-level feature added as an additive term.
notes: Ranking is within-user, so any term constant across a user's impressions cannot change that user's order. Contributes exactly zero. User information can only act through a cross with the item side.

score_transform.name: Per-user monotone score transforms
score_transform.summary: Calibration, sigmoid, per-user normalisation at inference.
notes: Both GAUC and nDCG@5 depend only on within-user order, which a monotone transform preserves. Exactly zero effect.

objective_bpr.name: Within-user pairwise (BPR) objective or auxiliary pairwise term
objective_bpr.summary: Sampled positive/negative pairs drawn within one user's impressions, either replacing the pointwise loss or added to it with a weight.
notes: REOPENED by the controlled objective ablation. Given the WINNING implementation's scaffolding, pairwise scores +0.00119 over the official baseline and +0.00359 over pointwise on identical batches, 3/3 seeds up. The five historical BPR misses were IMPLEMENTATION failures, not evidence against pairwise objectives.

Pairwise and listwise are not distinguishable here: listwise leads by +0.00043, worst seed -0.00001, 2/3 up -- inside the 0.0008 seed reference and far below the 0.0014 bar. Do not propose listwise over pairwise expecting a gain.
Scope: research/objective_ablation (3 objectives x 3 matched seeds, one model, one batching scheme, only the loss varied)

measured.note: delta exactly +0.00000: branch never activated -- see constraints.md C24
pairwise, A's scaffolding, +0.00359 vs pointwise on identical batches

objective_listwise.name: Within-user listwise softmax replacing pointwise BCE
objective_listwise.summary: Replace the pointwise BCE objective with a within-user listwise softmax (ListNet / Plackett-Luce style) over each user's training list.
notes: CONTROLLED ABLATION SETTLES THIS. Holding model, features, batching and seeds fixed and changing only the loss: pointwise 0.59905, pairwise 0.60263, listwise 0.60306. A RANKING OBJECTIVE beats pointwise by +0.00401 (3/3 seeds). LISTWISE beats PAIRWISE by only +0.00043 (2/3 seeds, worst -0.00001) -- indistinguishable.
So the gain belongs to "not pointwise", not to "listwise". The ablation reproduced the banked submission's hand-verified +0.00162 exactly, so this is measuring the right thing.

THE COST IS IN THE BATCHING. Grouping rows by user -- which the ranking losses require -- costs -0.00239 on its own (pointwise on grouped batches vs the official pointwise baseline). The net +0.00162 is a +0.00401 objective gain minus a -0.00239 batching loss. Recovering that -0.00239 is worth more than any further listwise variant.
Scope: research/objective_ablation (3 objectives x 3 matched seeds, one model, one batching scheme, only the loss varied)

measured.note: delta exactly +0.00000: branch never activated, config was dropped. NOT a measurement -- see constraints.md C24
VERIFIED +0.00162 mean over 3 matched seeds, all positive -- banked submission
listwise, A's scaffolding; reproduces the banked +0.00162 exactly

ablation.design: one model, one batching scheme, 3 matched seeds, only the loss varied
ablation.conclusion: a RANKING objective beats pointwise by +0.00401, but listwise beats pairwise by only +0.00043 (2/3 seeds, worst -0.00001) -- indistinguishable. The gain is "not pointwise", not "listwise". The user-grouped batching the ranking losses need costs -0.00239 on its own; recovering that is worth more than another loss variant.

objective_hybrid_listwise.name: Pointwise BCE plus a weighted within-user listwise term
objective_hybrid_listwise.summary: Keep the pointwise logloss on every row and add a weighted listwise softmax term.
notes: Two independent formulations, both several sigma negative. Lightly replicated (n=2) -- classified WEAK NEGATIVE in constraints.md C27, closed here because two independent misses is the registry bar.
Weights tested: 0.5 (with and without a 3-epoch warmup) and 0.3.

prior_user_aggregates.name: Strictly-prior USER-side behavioural aggregates as bucketized FM fields
prior_user_aggregates.summary: Count-smoothed prior long_view rates built from strictly earlier rows: a user-level engagement-rate bucket (acts only through its crosses), plus user-tab and user-author affinity buckets (which vary within a user's list).
notes: THE LARGEST SINGLE CONFIRMED GAIN IN ANY RUN: +0.00281 mean over 3 matched seeds, worst seed +0.00236, all three positive. Baseline 0.60147 -> 0.60609 as a 3-seed rank average. Gain is mainly GAUC (0.6674->0.6738).
Mechanism is C2-legal: user-tab and user-author vary within a list and reorder it first-order; the user-level rate is constant within a user and can only act through crosses with the item side.
Single investigation. Not yet independently replicated -- see constraints.md C28.

prior_item_aggregates.name: Strictly-prior ITEM-side and user-item identity-level aggregates
prior_item_aggregates.summary: Video prior long_view rate + support bucket, author prior rate + support bucket, user-author prior rate + support bucket, as bucketized categorical FM fields.
notes: Added ON TOP of the kept user-side aggregates it went the wrong way: -0.00320. The stated reasoning was that item-side priors should help MORE than user-side ones because they vary within a list; the measured sign refuted that.
A user-tab conditional prior rate plus a user-level prior play_time bucket, also on top of the kept model, gave -0.00333.

Six earlier runs that bundled user-side and item-side prior aggregates together were all negative (-0.00114 to -0.00229); those do not isolate the item side but are consistent with it. See constraints.md C29.

measured.note: video+author+user-author priors on top of the iter-4 model
user-tab conditional prior + user play_time bucket on top of iter 4

grouped_batching_cost.name: Recover the cost of user-grouped batching
grouped_batching_cost.summary: The ranking objectives need rows grouped by user. That grouping, with the loss held pointwise, measures -0.00239 against the official baseline. Anything that keeps the ranking objective while restoring the lost -0.00239 is worth more than a better ranking loss.
notes: Measured, 3 matched seeds: official pointwise (random batches) 0.601440; the same pointwise loss on user-grouped batches 0.599047. Only the batching differs.

Candidates not yet tested: larger target_bs so a batch holds more users; a pointwise term restored on ungrouped rows alongside the ranking term; group-order shuffling at a finer granularity; revisiting early stopping, since the grouped pointwise arm ran to epochs 8/11/10 against listwise 3/4/4.
Scope: research/objective_ablation (3 objectives x 3 matched seeds, one model, one batching scheme, only the loss varied)
